findings.documented: project_id links the listing to a builder project, and is null for resale property that is not part of one
findings.actual: listings sharing the same project_id are frequently in completely different buildings and locations. Example: project_id P40276 links listings from 4 different named buildings (Prestige Vista, SHRIRAM CREST, Rohan Park, Aparna Heights), 13-25 km apart despite all being tagged locality=velachery. The most extreme case found had linked listings 8,172 km apart. The project record for P40276 itself is named 'Brigade Meadows', which matches none of its 12 linked listings' apartment names.
findings.how_found: measured pairwise distances between listings sharing the same project_id, expecting them to be physically close since they claim to belong to the same builder project; found distances inconsistent with any real geographic grouping
findings.impact: project_id cannot be trusted to identify listings belonging to the same real building or project. This affects any analysis relying on project_id for grouping, including the reported total_listings count per project and identifying a project's actual price range

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: 867 of 4,100 retrievable listing records (21%) have is_live: false, meaning inactive listings are NOT excluded by the server as claimed. The is_live field itself is also undocumented — it does not appear anywhere in the documented listing object.
findings.how_found: counted is_live values across the full deduplicated dataset after confirming pagination correctness
findings.impact: a frontend trusting the documentation's claim would show inactive/withdrawn listings to users as if they were live and available, contradicting the stated 'safe to show to a user' guarantee
